identity.name: F-91W
identity.one_liner: A resin digital watch introduced in 1989 that has since sold over 100 million units, making it the most-produced watch in the world.

provenance_events.person_or_event: The Guardian: Guantánamo Bay files report
provenance_events.description: The Guardian reported that declassified Guantanamo Bay interrogation assessment documents, released via WikiLeaks, described the Casio F-91W as 'the sign of al-Qaida' because its timer function could be adapted for improvised explosive devices; the watch was cited in prisoner assessments roughly 150 times.

narrative.story: Designed by Ryusuke Moriai and introduced by Casio in June 1989, the F-91W has stayed in continuous production for over three decades on a formula of low price, long battery life, and an unchanged three-button digital layout. Cumulative production is estimated above 100 million units, making it the best-selling watch ever made. Its ubiquity has cut both ways: the same low cost and simple timer function that made it a favorite everyday watch also led declassified Guantanamo Bay documents to flag it as a marker associated with al-Qaeda bomb-making training.
narrative.collector_notes: Case, dial print, and module have changed little since 1989; collectors distinguish era mainly by the small print on the caseback and country of assembly rather than by any cosmetic revision.
